verification_report.summary: Both staged lemmas are correct under the explicitly stipulated internal premises. In the first lemma, the common competitor h makes every finite rooftop genuine across different ordinary singularity types. Disjoint first-contact pieces give the weighted estimate without asserting finite-index membership in E_phi or equality of masses. The decreasing tail envelopes and their increasing canonical limit stay above h and below a, so upward stability places them in E_phi. Their monotone capacity convergence and the bounded quasi-continuous weights justify both lower-semicontinuity passages. Zero domination identifies the limiting envelope with a; the upper-tail squeeze and subsequence criterion establish capacity convergence. In the second lemma, the exponential measure inequality follows from a,a_j <= u_j,v_j. Outside E_j, both a and a_j are <= -t_j, giving a remainder bounded by (4K/e) exp(-t_j/2), where K bounds the summed input masses. Fixed finite non-pluripolar integration is correctly applied to exponentials, yielding the required weighted self-error. For each fixed T, all locality and bounded-density claims hold on {chi_T>0}, where h,u,v,a_j,a exceed -2T; the cutoff vanishes at the boundary. Constant truncations are correctly handled in a larger Hermitian background, with signed bounded products and uniformly capacity-controlled total variations. The right-hand cutoff measures converge in total variation. Removing the cutoffs proves mu_a = exp(a-u)mu_u + exp(a-v)mu_v, whose right side is dominated by the finite measure mu_u+mu_v. This covers both-truncated, one-fixed, and both-fixed inputs even when the undamped weighted reference measure is infinite. BMP supplies the required finiteness, and positive lower reference volume enters through the stipulated domination theorem. The contextual [XL26 Proposition 6.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.13446v1) was checked after the required arXiv-theorem search; its conclusion is not used. No raw weak convergence of the uncut approximating measures is assumed or asserted. No critical errors or gaps were found.
